target: pistillate flower (PO_0025599) of the allomorphic kind: absent (PATO_0000462). Only this special form of female flower is missing; flowers in general are present.
fix: '<modifier> <part> absent' (allomorphic, sterile, staminate, pistillate, basal, cauline ...): the absence applies only to the modified kind of part (a subclass, or the part plus a context quality), never to the bare parent part.
reason: The absence of a special flower form was widened to 'flower absent' and then misannotated as 'flower: present'. The plant clearly has flowers, since its inflorescences are bisexual.

target: Annulus (ring at the mouth of the perianth tube) absent, on perianth (PO_0009058), not corolla. There is no class for this annulus because 'annulus' was rejected as a generic part, so leave it unannotated. 'syrinx present' also belongs to the perianth tube (PO_0009058), not the corolla.
fix: '<sub-part> absent/present' maps to the sub-part, not to its parent organ. If the sub-part word has no class (annulus, syrinx), drop the statement rather than moving the presence or absence onto the parent. In Aristolochiaceae, perianth-tube structures never map to corolla.
reason: Aristolochia has a single perianth (calyx) and no corolla. Both statements are about small structures of the perianth tube and were both put on corolla. The 'absent' became 'present', so these are two misreadings, not a contradiction in the plant.

target: colleter (FLOPO_0986023) on leaf lamina (PO_0020039): absent (PATO_0000462)
fix: '<organ-adjective> <part> absent' (laminar colleters, petiolar glands, marginal veins, basal leaves): the noun is the absent part and the adjective only says where it sits. Never put the absence on the organ the adjective names.
reason: The adjective 'laminar' was read as the bearer. The leaf blade is present and described (apex acute).

target: Only the lowest (basal) leaf sheaths (leaf sheath PO_0020104) lack a blade. Where the flora says the culm's basal sheaths are bladeless, use culm (stem PO_0009047) + aphyllopodic (FLOPO:0991233). Leaf lamina (PO_0020039) is present.
fix: 'bladeless' / 'bladeless sheaths' / 'sheaths bladeless' (sedges, grasses): the lowest sheaths have no blade. It is not the absence of leaf lamina for the taxon. Scope it to the basal sheaths, or use aphyllopodic on the culm.
reason: This is the documented pattern ('bladeless sheaths' read as 'leaf lamina absent'). The vegetative-shoot blades are described as filiform.

target: Caudex (woody perennial stem base) absent. PO has no separate caudex class; it is only a synonym of stem (PO_0009047), so leave it unannotated or use a stem-base phrasing. Stem: present.
fix: If a PO synonym names a special kind of the part (caudex, scape, culm, trunk, phyllodia, bracteole), its absence must not be read as absence of the parent class. Map 'caudex absent' / 'without a caudex' to no absence of stem.
reason: 'caudex' resolves to stem through the PO synonym list. The aerial stems are present and erect.

target: cauline leaf (PO_0000013): absent (PATO_0000462). The basal (rosette) leaves (PO_0000014) are present and sessile or petiolate.
fix: 'cauline leaves absent' → cauline leaf (PO_0000013) absent. 'basal leaves absent' → rosette leaf (PO_0000014) absent, or leaf + basal (FLOPO:0991002) absent. Never 'leaf absent'.
reason: The position word was dropped. The described leaves are the basal ones.

target: Axillary leaf clusters (secondary leaves on short axillary shoots) absent. There is no class for these, so leave unannotated. Leaf (PO_0009025) is present and connate at the base.
fix: 'axillary leaves absent' / 'without axillary fascicles' says the leaf axils have no secondary leaf clusters. It is not the absence of leaves. Scope it to the axillary short shoot, or drop it.
reason: In Minuartia this sentence contrasts with species that have leaf clusters in the axils. The main leaves are present and described.

target: phyllode leaf (PO_0025335): absent (PATO_0000462)
fix: Resolve 'phyllodia / phyllode(s) absent' to phyllode leaf (PO_0025335), the most specific class, not to its parent leaf.
reason: Sarracenia's flat non-pitcher leaves (phyllodia) are missing, but its pitcher leaves are present and green.

target: Peduncle (PO_0009053) bears no bracts, i.e. peduncle bracts absent. Involucral bracts (PO_0009045) are present.
fix: 'ebracteate / not bracteate / bractless' is a quality of the organ it follows (peduncle, pedicel, flower, inflorescence): that organ bears no bracts. Never read it as 'bract absent' for the whole plant, especially in Asteraceae, where phyllaries are always present.
reason: 'ebracteate' lost its subject (most likely the peduncle) and was turned into an absence of every bract, which clashes with the phyllaries.

target: Peduncle (PO_0009053) without sterile bracts. Floral bracts (flower bract PO_0009034) are present and longer than the ovary.
fix: '<organ> ebracteate' says only that the named organ bears no bracts. Bracts elsewhere (floral bracts) are not covered.
reason: The flora itself says the peduncle is ebracteate. The orchid's floral bracts are described.

target: leaf lamina intramarginal vein (PO_0025520): absent (PATO_0000462)
fix: 'marginal vein(s) absent' / 'without a marginal vein' → leaf lamina intramarginal vein (PO_0025520) absent. The adjective 'marginal' must not move the absence onto lamina or margin.
reason: The vein was dropped and the absence was put on the blade. The blade is present (apex acute).

target: Basal leaf sheaths (leaf sheath PO_0020104) without lamina, or culm (PO_0009047) + aphyllopodic (FLOPO:0991233). Leaf lamina (PO_0020039) is present and flat.
fix: 'bladeless sheaths' names sheaths that have no blade. It must not produce 'leaf lamina absent' for the taxon.
reason: Same case as the documented moss/sedge example. The blades are described as flat.

target: Flowering stem (stem PO_0009047) leafless, i.e. cauline leaf (PO_0000013) absent. The basal leaves are present.
fix: 'leafless' after a stem, scape, flowering stem or culm → cauline leaf (PO_0000013) absent. 'leafless' as a whole-plant term applies only when the flora says the plant is leafless.
reason: In Crepis, 'leafless' describes the scapose stems. The leaves are described (apex acute).

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106) absent (PATO_0000462). The other statement also belongs elsewhere: external (outer) ligule → ligule (PO_0020105), pubescent.
fix: In grasses and bamboos, 'auricle(s)' → leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106) and 'ligule' (inner or outer) → ligule (PO_0020105). Neither is ever stipule.
reason: Both bamboo sheath structures were mapped to stipule, which created the clash. Fargesia has no stipules.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106) absent; oral setae absent (no class; seta is not awn). The length 'ca. 2/3 as long as internodes' belongs to the culm sheath (leaf sheath PO_0020104), as a length relative to the internode (pattern 10).
fix: Bamboo 'auricles and oral setae absent' → sheath auricle absent and oral setae absent. Never map these to stipule, and never map 'setae' to awn here.
reason: Both statements are about sheath structures and were both placed on stipule.

target: Sterile (PATO_0000956) flowers (PO_0009046) absent, i.e. no marginal sterile flowers. Fertile flowers are present.
fix: A context word from flora_context_words.tsv (sterile, fertile, male, female, marginal, ray) before a part in an absence statement restricts the absence to that kind of part.
reason: In Hydrangea, 'sterile flowers absent' means the showy marginal flowers are missing. The inflorescence with fertile flowers is described.

target: No annotation: this is missing information, not an absence.
fix: 'not known / not seen / unknown / not observed / not collected / imperfectly known' → no annotation. Never record it as absent.
reason: The flowers were never collected. The species has fruiting cymes, so it certainly flowers.

target: No annotation: the flowers were not seen.
fix: 'flowers not seen' is a gap in what was collected → no annotation (same rule as 'not known').
reason: Missing data was read as absence. Racemes are described.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106): absent (PATO_0000462); oral setae: absent (no class)
fix: In a list ending in 'absent' ('A and B absent', 'A, B and C absent'), apply the absence to every member. The first noun must not come out as 'present'.
reason: The same sentence produced both annotations. The auricles lost the negation that applies to the whole list.

target: Context: which floret or spikelet. The lower lemma (or the pedicelled spikelet) is awnless; the upper lemma has a geniculate awn.
fix: 'awnless' qualified by lower or upper floret, lemma, glume or spikelet (sessile/pedicelled) applies only to that member. Carry the member into the annotation and never write 'awn absent' for the taxon.
reason: In Ischaemum, awns differ between florets and spikelets. The flora states that the upper lemma is awned.

target: frond (FLOPO_0985026) sessile (PATO_0001436), i.e. FLOPO_0992054 'frond sessile'. The frond is present.
fix: 'without <part> at <place>' gives the absence of the named part (here the stalk). It never gives the absence of the subject the sentence describes. Lemna 'frond' → FLOPO_0985026, not leaf.
reason: The stalk was dropped and the absence was put on the frond (read as leaf). The frond is described (papillae).

target: 'linear' belongs to the bracteoles of the umbellets: bracteole (PO_0009043) linear (PATO_0001199). The absence 'bracts absent' should be scoped to the umbel's involucral bracts (involucral bract PO_0009045).
fix: Apiaceae: 'bracts' = involucral bracts of the umbel (PO_0009045) and 'bracteoles' = bracts of the umbellets (PO_0009043). Do not let 'bracteole' fall back to bract (PO_0009055) through the PO synonym.
reason: Apiaceae descriptions normally read 'bracts absent; bracteoles ... linear'. 'bracteole' is a PO synonym of bract, so the bracteoles were annotated as bract.

target: Context: which sheath. The culm sheath has no auricles; the foliage-leaf sheath has elliptic or falcate auricles (or the reverse, per the source).

target: Context: flower type. The chasmogamous (open) flowers have obovate petals; the cleistogamous (closed, self-pollinating) flowers have no petals.
fix: 'petals absent' in a sentence about cleistogamous, closed, female or lower flowers applies only to that flower type. Keep the flower-type context and never write 'petal absent' for the taxon.
reason: Pseudostellaria typically has two flower types, and the closed ones have no petals.

target: rosette leaf (PO_0000014) absent (PATO_0000462), or leaf + basal (FLOPO:0991002) absent. The cauline leaves are present and glabrous.
fix: 'basal leaves absent' → rosette leaf / basal leaf absent only.

target: No bracts at the base of the involucre or on the peduncle (involucre not calyculate). Involucral bracts (PO_0009045) are present, with broad scarious margins.
fix: In Asteraceae, 'not bracteate / ebracteate / without bracteoles' after an involucre, capitulum or peduncle means no outer calyculus bracts or peduncle bracts. It never means the phyllaries are absent.

target: Leaves (PO_0009025) present, crowded at the stem apex and distant (remote). No absence.
fix: 'leafless except at/near <place>', 'leafy only above' → leaves present at that place. Any '<absence> except ...' wording is not an absence.
reason: The 'except at apex' part was lost, so a positional statement became an absence.

target: bracteole (PO_0009043): absent (PATO_0000462). The bracts at the base of the peduncle are present.
fix: 'bracteolate / not bracteolate / ebracteolate' → bracteole (PO_0009043), never bract (PO_0009055), even though PO lists 'bracteole' as a synonym of bract.

target: Stem (PO_0009047) with few leaves: cauline leaf (PO_0000013) decreased amount (PATO_0001997). Not absent.
fix: 'almost / nearly / subleafless', 'almost glabrous' and similar: 'almost' + absence → reduced amount (PATO_0001997) or no annotation. Never absent.
reason: The word 'almost' was dropped. Oblanceolate leaves are described.

target: lower glume (PO_0006002): absent (PATO_0000462). The upper glume is present.
fix: 'lower/upper/first/second glume absent' → that glume only (lower glume PO_0006002). The same goes for 'lower lemma', 'lower floret' and similar.
